angle: y'=y read as a direction field filling the plane, so that exp is the unique integral curve through (0,1) — with the one-line uniqueness proof g=f·e^{-x}, g'=0, MVT ⇒ g constant, staged against a user-supplied candidate f

libraries.name: paper.js
libraries.role: vector scene graph for all six direction-field canvases and two plot canvases: layered arrow lattice / integral-curve polylines / hover overlay, plus Path.simplify() Bezier fitting of the freehand stroke and getPointAt+getTangentAt for its analytic tangents (the quantity compared against the field)

libraries.name: mathjs
libraries.role: parse the user's candidate f(x), differentiate it symbolically (math.derivative + math.simplify), emit TeX for f and f', and compile both to numeric evaluators so the verdict max|f'-f| and the plot of g=f·e^{-x} are computed from the typed expression

libraries.name: katex
libraries.role: typeset all static statements (data-tex attributes) and all dynamic ones (proof steps, live e^{x+s}=e^s e^x identity, symbolic f and f')

building_blocks: Frame: world<->view affine transform with per-side padding, rebuilt on resize (vx/vy/wx/wy)

FieldView: reusable direction-field component — own PaperScope per canvas, four layers (axes/field/curves/overlay), slope callback (x,y)=>m, arrow lattice with arrowheads, magnitude+sign colour ramp, curves stored in WORLD coords and re-projected on resize, pointer->world helper

PlotView: light-theme function plot component — nice 1/2/5·10^n tick stepper, autoscaled y window with a minimum span so a constant function still reads as flat, polyline with out-of-range gap splitting, dashed horizontal reference line, inline text labels
rk4/heun/euler stepper factory + forward-and-backward integrator with |y| and x-range bailouts
deviation(): max absolute and max relative error of a numerical trace against a closed form
one-shot curve trace animation via view.onFrame with a setTimeout completion guarantee (survives throttled rAF / background tabs / headless capture)
freehand capture -> world-coordinate raw stroke -> Paper Path.simplify() refit -> resampled tangent-vs-field angle error -> per-segment colour ramp (obey/drift/disobey)
staged proof stepper: array of {line, tex, why} with prev/next, progress dots, KaTeX per step, and a step index that drives what the companion plot annotates
KaTeX helpers: renderToString wrapper K(tex,display) + typeset() sweep over [data-tex]/[data-display] elements

fold-down section layout: sticky nav bar, numbered sections, 2-column split (canvas card | argument), dark canvas 'stage' cards on a light paper page, note/warn/cool callouts, monospace data tables, verdict banners
computations: direction field: slope m = k*y evaluated on a lattice, normalised in SCREEN space so arrows have constant pixel length
classical RK4 integration of y' = k y forward and backward from an arbitrary release point (h = 0.01)
forward Euler and Heun/RK2 integration of the same field at selectable step sizes (h = 0.05, 0.25, 1)
max |numeric - c e^{k(x-x0)}| and max relative error for every traced curve, recomputed per boat
e read off the traced gold path at x = 1 (2.718281828) rather than taken from Math.E
c = y0 e^{-x0} for each release point
symbolic derivative f' of a user-typed expression, and symbolic f' - f
numeric residual max |f'(x) - f(x)| over 601 samples on [-2,2] as the verdict on whether f solves the law
g(x) = f(x) e^{-x} sampled on [-2,2] with its total range, so 'g is constant' is a measurement

freehand stroke: analytic Bezier tangents at 261 offsets, screen-space angle between the drawn tangent and the field direction, arc-length fraction within tolerance, max |y'_drawn - y|, max vertical gap to e^x, count of near-vertical (not-a-graph) samples
e^{x+s} vs e^s e^x drawn from independent samplings to show they coincide
half-life / doubling length ln2/|k| for the y' = k y field
interactions: hover the field (section 1): a large gold arrow follows the pointer, the isocline y = const is dashed in and its arrows redrawn in white, readout gives (x,y) and the demanded slope
click anywhere in the field (section 2): drops a boat, traces its integral curve with a one-shot animation, appends a row with c and the measured deviation from c·e^x
buttons: drop at (0,1), drop a column of 7 boats at x=-1, mirror below the axis, the equilibrium y=0, clear
shift slider s and a reflect checkbox (section 3): moves e^{x+s}, draws e^s·e^x on top of it, updates the live KaTeX identity and c = ±e^s

freehand pointer drawing (section 4): draw a curve, release to have it fitted and painted by tangent disagreement; tolerance selector (4/8/15 degrees) and an overlay toggle for the true e^x re-judge in place
candidate f (section 5): preset dropdown or free-text expression, Enter or 'plot it' re-derives f' symbolically and redraws both f and g = f·e^{-x} with a pass/fail verdict
proof stepper (section 5): prev/next through 9 steps; from step 7 the g-plot gains the dashed f(0) constant line
integration method selector (section 6): RK4/Heun/Euler at h = 0.01/0.05/0.25/1 redraws the numerical trace against the dashed exact curve and rewrites the measured-error table
k slider (section 7): rebuilds the whole direction field for y' = k y, retraces the family and e^{kx}, reports the doubling/halving length and a matching real-world caption
window resize: every view re-projects its stored world-coordinate curves, and the freehand stroke is re-fitted and re-judged rather than discarded
assets: katex .woff2 fonts (20 files in lib/katex/fonts, referenced by katex.min.css via relative url(fonts/...))
gotchas: paper-core.min.js (not paper-full) is the right build for JS-driven use: paper-full bundles acorn for PaperScript, which is dead weight when you never write a <script type='text/paperscript'> block

one PaperScope per canvas is required for multiple canvases, and because Path/Layer constructors insert into the ACTIVE project you must call scope.activate() before creating any item — every draw method here starts with it

Paper.js items live in view (CSS pixel) coordinates, so curves must be stored in world coordinates and re-projected on resize, otherwise everything drifts when the layout changes; the same applies to the freehand stroke, which is kept as world-space raw points and re-fitted

view.onFrame animations are not guaranteed to run (background tab, throttled rAF, headless screenshot) — the one-shot trace pairs the frame loop with a setTimeout that force-completes the path, otherwise curves can be left half-drawn

Path.simplify() on a nearly straight stroke can legitimately return a 2-segment path; guarding on segments.length < 3 silently kills the whole freehand measurement (use arc length, not segment count, as the 'too short' test)
an overlay helper that clears its layer must not be called after the content you want to keep has been drawn into it — the start-marker helper takes an explicit clear flag for this reason
mathjs ships an ESM-only 'main' but lib/browser/math.js is a UMD bundle that sets window.math, which is what file:// needs; the jsDelivr path must point at lib/browser/math.js explicitly
math.derivative throws on expressions it has no rule for; the candidate analyser falls back to a central-difference derivative and says so in the UI rather than failing silently
math.simplify does not always reduce a genuinely-zero difference to '0', so the pass/fail verdict is driven by the numeric residual max|f'-f| and the symbolic f'-f is only displayed as corroboration
mathjs returns Complex objects for e.g. sqrt(-1) rather than NaN, so sample loops must test isFinite() and skip rather than assume a number
KaTeX refuses to render in quirks mode — the file must start with <!DOCTYPE html>
there is no katex auto-render extension vendored: static math is declared with data-tex attributes and swept once on load, dynamic math via katex.renderToString
